predict_steps.prompt: You start a flood at the first land cell (0,0). After the flood finishes, which cells are in visited for that island?
accepted_answers: the 2x2 block of 1s in the top-left
four cells in the top-left island
predict_steps.hint: Four-direction flood stays inside the contiguous block of 1s.

predict_steps.prompt: After finishing that island, the scan finds the next unvisited land. What is its (r, c)?
predict_steps.hint: Row-major scan; the lone 1 in the middle row.

viva.question: Why is DFS or BFS flood-fill linear in the number of grid cells?
expected_points: each cell is marked visited at most once
every edge to a neighbor is examined a constant number of times
islands are counted only when a new unvisited land cell starts a flood
water cells are skipped without expanding

viva.question: What is the answer on an all-water grid?
expected_points: no land cell with value one appears

viva.question: Why mark a cell visited when you start flooding it?
expected_points: otherwise the same land would be counted again
neighbor expansion must not revisit the cell
the component becomes a single connected region under that mark
deferred marking can explode into repeated searches
